Drier southwesterlies are expected to continue across the Marianas
overnight, with another surge in the monsoon along with embedded
disturbances to more likely bring a peak in shower and thunder
coverage to the area around midweek. Conditions are expected to
improve considerably in the second half of the week, with only low-
end scattered showers expected through at least Columbus Day.
Developing Tropical Depression Koguma (27W) over the Marshall
Islands, is not expected to bring any direct impacts to the Marianas
at this time, but mariners may need to continue to monitor the
situation if any distant swells will arrive from the northeast by 
the next weekend.

Marine...
Combined seas have fallen below 10 feet, but winds are expected to 
remain strong enough to remain hazardous to small craft overnight, 
before likely dropping below hazardous levels thereafter. Now that 
distant STY Choi-wan (26W) continues to exit our region well to our 
north and the southwestern monsoon surge has weakened, this has 
allowed southwesterly and northerly swells to diminish enough to no 
longer produce hazardous surf along south, west and north facing 
reefs of the Marianas. As such, the High Surf Advisory and High Rip 
Current Risk Statement were allowed to expired earlier this 
afternoon. From now on, a moderate risk of rip currents is expected 
along south, west, and north facing reefs of the Marianas for at 
least the next several days.

Tropical Systems...
Super Typhoon Choi-wan (26W) is centered near 26N146E well east-
northeast of Iwo To. Choi-wan has been heading in a generally 
northward direction at about 13 mph, with maximum sustained winds of 
155 mph earlier today, which made it a Category 4 Typhoon. Choi-wan 
is forecast to weaken the next day or so, but will remain a Super 
Typhoon as it continues to move away from NWS Guam's Area of 
Responsibility (AOR).

Typhoon Nolo (15E) is centered near 25N178E, having entered NWS 
Guam's AOR just recently from the central Pacific while retaining its
name and designation since its inception in the eastern Pacific. 
Nolo was moving west at around 17 mph, continuing on this trajectory
for the next few days. Maximum sustained winds were 115 mph. By 
Thursday, Nolo is expected to collide with a massive marine front in 
the wake of Choi-wan becoming extra-tropical, to then get torn apart 
within the mid-latitude frictional forces off the coast of Japan by 
the next weekend.

Tropical Depression Koguma (27W), formerly known as JTWC's Invest 
94W, is centered near 11N168E right over Rongelap in the northern 
Marshalls. Recent ASCAT passes indicate a large swath of 25-30 kt 
winds spanning the southern peripheries of Koguma, further enhancing
its consolidation as it continues moving northward. Koguma will 
continue moving north and away from eastern Micronesia, heading 
toward the expected storm path of Typhoon Nolo (15E) by midweek, to 
then pivot to the northwest making a pass near Wake Island in the 
second half of the week. This system is not expected to produce any
TS impacts across eastern Micronesia at this time.

For more information, please refer to bulletins from the Joint 
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO headers WTPN31 PGTW, WTPN32 PGTW and
WTPN33 PGTW, and public advisories from the National Weather Service
under WMO headers WTPQ31 PGUM, WTPQ32 PGUM and WTPQ33 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
What was formerly Invest 94W has strengthened into TD Koguma (27W).
It's currently located just east of Rongelap in the northern RMI.
Visible imagery earlier today showed that most of the convection in 
the shape of a comma around the LLCC (Low-Level Circulation Center).
However, the latest visible imagery shows strengthening inflow into 
Koguma with convective growth increasing in the eastern through 
southern flanks of the TD, with it maintaining a comma shape. The 
latest forecast from JTWC (the Joint Typhoon Warning Center indicates
Koguma will become a tropical storm tonight, but with the LLCC and 
its associated tropical storm force winds removed from utirik and 
other nearby warning points, as the wind field will be north- 
northwest of the northern-most RMI.

However, the effects of the strengthening system in terms of an
increasing northerly swell will develop for the latter half of the
week, with a northwest to west swell also increasing a foot or so as
wave energy from Super Typhoon Choi-wan (nor west-northwest of
Minamitorishima) arriving. Given the wave period of 6 to 8 seconds
expected, this is just below high surf criteria for western reefs,
with really the bulk of it being northwesterly (310 degrees roughly)
at Pohnpei, and briefly touching 6 feet (maybe) at Kosrae. As such,
no headlines were issued/needed.
